meaning: Lamech's age when Noah was born – expectation of comfort and rest
description: The number 182 appears in Genesis 5:28, where it states that Lamech was 182 years old when he had his son Noah. In the genealogy from Adam to Noah, this marks an important point: Lamech gives his son the name Noah and connects it with a hope of relief from the heavy labor caused by the cursed ground (Gen 5:29). Thus, the number 182 carries a biblical context of expectation and prophetic hope, as Noah’s birth points forward to the coming judgment and renewal through the flood. Although the number has not developed a broad independent symbolic tradition, its placement in primeval history gives it clear theological grounding.

versions.meaning: The number 182 has no well-established or prominent symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition.
versions.description: 182 is not a number that is particularly highlighted in the Bible or in classical Jewish numerology (gematria) with an acknowledged symbolic role. It may be noted that 182 is the age of Jacob (Israel) according to Genesis 47:28, where he lived 147 years – but some traditions link 182 to Lamech, Noah's father, who was 182 years old when Noah was born according to Genesis 5:28. This gives the number a certain biblical context connected with expectation and hope for comfort, since the name Noah means "rest" or "comfort", but the number itself has not developed a strong independent symbolic tradition.
versions.reason: [critical] The Description contains incorrect information: it first states that 182 is the lifespan of Jacob (147 years) – this is directly contradictory and confusing. Jacob's age was 147 years (Gen 47:28), not 182. The sentence is self-contradictory.; [major] The Meaning field says the number has no well-established symbolic significance, but 182 has a clear and direct biblical occurrence as Lamech's age when Noah was born (Gen 5:28). This should be reflected better in the meaning.; [major] The Description is messy and uncertain in tone ('may be mentioned', 'some traditions'). The connection to Lamech and Noah's birth is not speculative – it is stated explicitly in Genesis 5:28. The text should be rewritten to be clearer and more confident about this connection.; [minor] Interesting facts about the name Noah and its meaning ('rest/comfort') as well as the context in the genealogy fit well as footnotes to improve the flow of the description.

footnotes.text: The name Noah (נֹחַ) is related to the Hebrew verb נוח (nuach), which means "to rest." Lamech said: "He will comfort us in our work and the toil of our hands on the ground that the Lord has cursed" (Gen 5:29).

In the biblical chronology of Genesis 5, the genealogies from Adam to Noah form a carefully structured timeline. Lamech's 182 years at Noah's birth places this moment within a chain of patriarchal ages that together make up the period from creation to the flood.

Some rabbinic commentators view the genealogies in Genesis 5 as carriers of theological meaning, where each patriarch's name and age point toward God's plan of salvation. Lamech's prophetic statement at Noah's birth is interpreted as an expression of messianic longing.
